items.title: 14.1.8 Direction Angles and Direction Cosines of a Vector (Roman Urdu)

blocks.title: Numbering note
blocks.text: Kitab is heading ko 14.1.9 chhaapti hai (Book# 14.1.9). Kitab mein 14.1.1 naam ki koi heading hai hi nahin, is liye portal 14.1 ke sub-headings ko tarteeb se 14.1.1 se 14.1.8 tak number karta hai. Yahan 14.1.8 wahi hai jo kitab mein 14.1.9 hai.

Bachon, kisi vector ki simt kaise bataayein? Plane mein ek angle kaafi tha (x-axis se kitna ghooma hua hai). Space mein teen axes hain, is liye hum teen angles lete hain: vector ka x-axis, y-axis aur z-axis ke saath angle. Yeh direction angles kehlate hain, aur un ke cosines direction cosines. Is subtopic ka sab se khoobsurat nateeja yeh hai ke in teen cosines ke squares ka jama hamesha 1 hota hai.

Farz karein \(\underline{r} = \underline{OP} = x\underline{i} + y\underline{j} + z\underline{k}\) ek non-zero vector hai, aur \(\alpha\), \(\beta\) aur \(\gamma\) tarteeb se \(\underline{r}\) aur unit coordinate vectors \(\underline{i}\), \(\underline{j}\) aur \(\underline{k}\) ke darmiyan angles hain, jahan \(0 \le \alpha \le \pi\), \(0 \le \beta \le \pi\) aur \(0 \le \gamma \le \pi\).

blocks.alt: Axes x, y, z from O with short unit vectors i, j, k along them. An arrow r goes from O to a point P, with dashed lines showing its coordinates. Arcs mark the angle alpha between r and the x-axis, beta between r and the y-axis, and gamma between r and the z-axis.
blocks.caption: Direction angles α, β, γ of r = OP with i, j, k (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.text: Figure ko ghaur se dekhiye: vector \(\underline{r}\) origin se nikal kar point \(P\) tak jaata hai. Har axis ke saath us ka ek angle hai: x-axis ke saath \(\alpha\), y-axis ke saath \(\beta\) aur z-axis ke saath \(\gamma\). Ek aasaan tasawwur: kamre ke kone se chhat ki taraf ek lakri tirchi rakhi ho, to woh farsh ke dono kinaron aur khare kinare, teenon se alag alag angle banati hai. Yahi teen angles mil kar lakri ki simt poori tarah bata dete hain.

items: Angles \(\alpha\), \(\beta\) aur \(\gamma\) ko direction angles (simt ke angles) kehte hain.
Numbers \(\cos\alpha\), \(\cos\beta\) aur \(\cos\gamma\) ko vector \(\underline{r}\) ke direction cosines kehte hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yeh teen angles batate hain ke vector har axis se kitna hat kar jhuka hua hai. Har angle \(0\) aur \(\pi\) (\(0^{\circ}\) se \(180^{\circ}\)) ke darmiyan hota hai; \(90^{\circ}\) se bara angle ka matlab hai ke woh component negative hai.
Misaal: \(\underline{r} = \underline{k}\) seedha upar hai: \(\gamma = 0^{\circ}\), \(\alpha = \beta = 90^{\circ}\), is liye direction cosines \(0, 0, 1\).
Kyun non-zero: zero vector ki koi simt nahin hoti, is liye us ke direction angles bhi nahin.
Important Result
Saabit kijiye ke \(\cos^{2}\alpha + \cos^{2}\beta + \cos^{2}\gamma = 1\).
Proof: farz karein

blocks.text_alt: r equals x, y, z equals x i plus y j plus z k
therefore magnitude of r equals square root of x squared plus y squared plus z squared, which we call r

blocks.text: to \(\dfrac{\underline{r}}{|\underline{r}|} = \left[\dfrac{x}{r}, \dfrac{y}{r}, \dfrac{z}{r}\right]\) vector \(\underline{r} = \underline{OP}\) ki simt (direction) mein unit vector hai (14.1.5 ka \(\hat{u} = \dfrac{\underline{u}}{|\underline{u}|}\)).

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab yahan "in the director of the vector" likhti hai; sahi "in the direction of the vector" hai.

blocks.alt: Axes x, y, z from O. The point P(x, y, z) is joined to O by a solid arrow, to A(x, 0, 0) on the x-axis by a dotted line, and to B(0, y, 0) on the y-axis and C(0, 0, z) on the z-axis by cyan lines. Arcs at O mark the angles alpha, beta and gamma that OP makes with the x-, y- and z-axes.
blocks.caption: P(x, y, z) with its feet A(x, 0, 0), B(0, y, 0), C(0, 0, z) on the axes; B is labelled (0, y, 0), see the correction (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab ki figure mein y-axis wale point par \(B(0, \gamma, 0)\) likha hai. Yeh point \(P(x, y, z)\) ka y-axis par paaon (foot) hai, is liye sahi label \(B(0, y, 0)\) hai; \(\gamma\) ek angle hai, coordinate nahin. Hamari figure mein sahi label hai.
Figure se nazar aata hai ke triangle \(OAP\) ek right triangle hai jis mein \(m\angle A = 90^{\circ}\). Is liye right triangle \(OAP\) mein (cos = saath wala side / hypotenuse):

blocks.text_alt: cos alpha equals OA over OP equals x over r

blocks.text: isi tarah

blocks.text_alt: cos beta equals y over r, cos gamma equals z over r

blocks.alt: A right triangle O A P with the right angle at A. The horizontal side OA has length x, the hypotenuse OP is the vector r, and the angle alpha is at O.
blocks.caption: Right triangle OAP: cos α = OA/OP = x/r (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Kyun: \(A\) par right angle kyun? \(A(x, 0, 0)\) x-axis par hai aur \(\underline{AP} = [0, y, z]\) ka x-component sifar hai, yani \(AP\) x-axis (aur \(OA\)) par perpendicular hai. Bilkul isi tarah \(B\) aur \(C\) se right triangles \(OBP\) aur \(OCP\) bante hain, jin se \(\cos\beta = y/r\) aur \(\cos\gamma = z/r\) milte hain.
Agar \(x\) negative ho tab bhi \(\cos\alpha = x/r\) sahi hai: us waqt \(\alpha\) obtuse (\(90^{\circ}\) se bara) hota hai aur \(\cos\alpha < 0\).
Numbers \(\cos\alpha = \dfrac{x}{r}\), \(\cos\beta = \dfrac{y}{r}\) aur \(\cos\gamma = \dfrac{z}{r}\) ko \(\underline{OP}\) ke direction cosines kehte hain. Ab in ke squares jama karte hain:

blocks.text_alt: cos squared alpha plus cos squared beta plus cos squared gamma equals x squared over r squared plus y squared over r squared plus z squared over r squared
equals x squared plus y squared plus z squared over r squared equals r squared over r squared equals 1

blocks.text: Kyun: pehli line mein teenon cosines ki values rakhi, doosri mein common denominator \(r^{2}\) liya, aur kyunke \(r = \sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2}}\) hai is liye \(x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2} = r^{2}\). Upar neeche same, jawab 1. Saabit ho gaya.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Direction cosines bilkul unit vector \(\hat{r}\) ke components hain: \(\hat{r} = \cos\alpha\,\underline{i} + \cos\beta\,\underline{j} + \cos\gamma\,\underline{k}\). \(\hat{r}\) ki lambai 1 hai, is liye us ke components ke squares ka jama 1 hai; yahi Important Result hai, ek doosre zaawiye se.
Is nateeje ka istemaal: teen angles kisi vector ke direction angles tabhi ho sakte hain jab un ke cosines ke squares ka jama 1 ho. \(45^{\circ}, 45^{\circ}, 60^{\circ}\) ke liye \(\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{4} = \frac{5}{4}\), is liye yeh mumkin nahin.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
(Hamari practice.) \(\underline{r} = 2\underline{i} - 3\underline{j} + 6\underline{k}\) ke direction cosines.
\(r = \sqrt{4 + 9 + 36} = \sqrt{49} = 7\)
\(\cos\alpha = \frac{2}{7}\), \(\cos\beta = -\frac{3}{7}\), \(\cos\gamma = \frac{6}{7}\)
Tasdeeq: \(\frac{4}{49} + \frac{9}{49} + \frac{36}{49} = \frac{49}{49} = 1\). \(\cos\beta\) negative hai, is liye \(\beta\) obtuse hai: vector y-axis se door, ulti taraf jhuka hai.

blocks.title: Dhyan dein
blocks.text: Exam mein aksar sawal aata hai: \"kya yeh teen angles kisi vector ke direction angles ho sakte hain?\" Is ka tareeqa hamesha ek hi hai: teenon angles ke cosines nikaaliye, un ke squares jama kijiye, aur dekhiye ke jawab 1 aata hai ya nahin. 1 aaye to haan, warna nahin. Jaise \(60^{\circ}, 60^{\circ}, 45^{\circ}\): \(\frac{1}{4} + \frac{1}{4} + \frac{1}{2} = 1\), is liye haan. Yaad rakhiye \(\cos 60^{\circ} = \frac{1}{2}\), \(\cos 45^{\circ} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\), \(\cos 90^{\circ} = 0\).

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
\(\underline{i} + \underline{j} + \underline{k}\) ke teenon direction angles barabar kyun hain, aur har ek kitna hai?
Jawab: teenon components barabar (1) hain, is liye teenon cosines \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\) hain. Angle \(\cos^{-1}\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\) hai, taqreeban 54.7 degree. Tasdeeq: \(\frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{3} = 1\).

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
Direction angles \(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\): \(\underline{r}\) ke \(\underline{i}, \underline{j}, \underline{k}\) ke saath angles, har ek \(0\) se \(\pi\).
Direction cosines: \(\cos\alpha = \frac{x}{r}\), \(\cos\beta = \frac{y}{r}\), \(\cos\gamma = \frac{z}{r}\), jahan \(r = |\underline{r}|\).
Yeh unit vector \(\hat{r}\) ke components hain.
\(\cos^{2}\alpha + \cos^{2}\beta + \cos^{2}\gamma = 1\).

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
Ghalat number se divide karna: har component magnitude \(r\) se divide hota hai, \(x + y + z\) se nahin.
Sign chhor dena: \(x < 0\) ho to \(\cos\alpha\) negative aur \(\alpha\) obtuse hai.
Squares ki jagah cosines jama kar dena: \(\cos\alpha + \cos\beta + \cos\gamma\) aam taur par 1 nahin hota.
